title: Local coach loses wager, treats team to pedicures - NewsBreak
text: PANAMA CITY, Fla. (WMBB) – What began as a simple incentive quickly turned into a $600 nail salon tab after the Rip City Surf 07 girls club soccer team scored seven goals, winning a bet placed by head coach Jona Hammond. “It was our second game of the tournament, so we needed to win to take the lead,” rising senior Hannah Bean said. “Then we started winning, but we clearly could’ve done better, so he was just trying to motivate us.” Despite holding a 2–0 lead at halftime, Hammond said he knew the team was not playing to its full potential. “I didn’t think they were playing well at all. I thought the other team had chances to score. It felt like a close game,” Hammond said. Originally, the incentive was simple: score two more goals, and the team would earn a pizza party. On the flip side, failure meant extra fitness training. But after the discussion, the girls made a counter-offer. “Two goals, pizza party. Three goals, ice cream. Chick-fil-A for the girls. And then, five goals, We all get a pedicure,” Hammond recalled. “I didn’t think there was any possible way that was going to happen. I watched them play in the first half.” What happened next was unexpected. The two-goal lead turned into a 7–0 shutout, and a sizable bill. “He calculated how much it would cost on the bench during the game and fell onto the ground,” North Bay Haven rising senior Lauren Bishop said. “It’s going to be expensive, because he’s paying for like 15 girls.” Nails were painted, and lessons were learned. “Six hundred dollars later, here we are. If you’re a coach,” Hammond said, “don’t ever do that.” For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to mypanhandle.com.
